messages:
sarah (Sales): FYI acme asked if we can run Private deploy behind their F5 + tenant proxy and keep client IP for logging. also want costs impact for a dedicated egress lane vs standard PrivateLink.

anika (SE): Quick Qs — is traffic mTLS terminated at their F5 or does it pass through to our infra?

acme_netops: (external) we terminate TLS at F5. then we SNI-proxy to your privatelink endpoint. source IP is important for fraud detection.

anika (SE): thanks. if TLS terminates at F5 then typical flow will NAT at their proxy. preserving client src IP across PrivateLink is not possible unless they forward original IP via header — do they support X-Forwarded-For?

acme_netops: They can inject headers yes, but security team wants guarantee and HSM/KMS compliance.

derek (NetEng): Options:
1) Transit via TGW + GWLB in front of our Private VPC to terminate and preserve paths (requires customer to route back to us, still NAT for source IP unless we use GRE/IPIP and preserve original — messy).
2) Use an app-proxy (customer ingress passes XFF) + app-level trust (validate header).
3) BYOIP + BGP route for source preservation (complex, rarely accepted).

anika (SE): I'd recommend option 2 for fastest POC. We can accept X-Forwarded-For and map to audit logs. For strict source-IP requirement we can propose a custom connector (extra eng effort + pricing).

priya (Security): Security notes: if they inject headers we need to validate header authenticity (HMAC or mTLS between F5 and our inbound proxy). Also need SOC2 proof for KMS usage. We should add an allowlist for their F5 IPs on the PrivateLink endpoint.

sarah (Sales): price ask — what's the delta for a connector + dedicated GWLB lane vs standard PrivateLink? ballpark numbers pls.

derek (NetEng): Ballpark: standard PrivateLink: no infra lift, normal per-GB egress. Dedicated GWLB lane / reserved capacity: ~ $12k/mo + per-hour reserved infra cost (depends on throughput). We'll surface exact once we size peak tokens/sec. For POC we can do a short-term reserved instance + pass-through pricing.

anika (SE): POC checklist (short):
- customer to provide F5 egress IPs and XFF header config
- mutual TLS cert bundle for our inbound proxy
- security HMAC secret for header validation
- allowlist inbound on PrivateLink endpoint (we'll provide target ENIs)
- sample curl test with header: `curl -H "X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4" https://privatedeploy.example/v1/generate`
- logging: we'll surface original header into audit logs/console

priya (Security): Add to checklist: KMS key policy exchange + retention SLA for logs.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: privatedeploy-test-env -> staging at 2024-06-12T14:00Z

sarah (Sales): ok i'll loop in acme procurement on pricing and push for header-handoff. @anika can you draft the minimal security config we need to give them?

anika (SE): will do. i'll post a one-pager with commands and firewall snippets in this thread within the hour. :thumbsup:

acme_netops: thanks all, we'll confirm XFF and send certs once we get procurement sign-off.

anika (SE): quick firewall snippet for their team (AWS SG example):
```
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Source: 198.51.100.0/24  # customer F5 egress
Description: Allow F5 toward PrivateLink ENI
```

anika (SE): and on our side we'll require inbound mTLS to our proxy at port 8443 and a host allowlist. We'll also validate HMAC on XFF header.

sarah (Sales): great — saved. we'll use this for the pricing attachment. cc: @priya (Security) for sign-off.

priya (Security): LGTM, will review the one-pager after anika posts it.

anika (SE): uploaded one-pager: https://redwood.example/s3/poc-f5-connector-spec.pdf

sarah (Sales): thanks team. next: deliverable= one-pager + price delta + POC runbook. target: EOW.
